'''Movistar R7''' is a professional League of Legends team from Latin America. They are co-owned by the American toy company [https://www.justtoysintl.com/ Just Toys]. They were previously known as '''Rainbow7'''.

== History ==
After being renamed, the 11 times champion of Latin America North at the time, continued to reign with an iron fist.

Despite the suspension of [[WhiteLotus]] that hindered their preparation for LLN Opening 2018 and their first Playoffs elimination in LLN Closing 2018, their mission to grow both within and outside their region remained intact. With this in mind, their actions at the international level had given them the prestige and respect from all the regions that were known as emerging. 

After the departure of their famous roster, the organization adquired a new roster for the first LLA split. The roster counted with players from former rival [[Dash9 Gaming]] and other Latin American Teams. This roster included: [[Acce]], [[Grell]], [[Leza]], [[Nobody (Nicolás Ale)|Nobody]], and [[Baula]]. This team reached the LLA Opening Finals, but lost against [[Isurus]] in a 3-1. After that, [[Grell]] and [[Baula]] left the team and [[Spooky (Miroslav Gochev)|Spooky]] and [[Tulz]] joined the team. The team reached playoffs but lost 3-0 against [[INFINITY|Infinity Esports]]. At the end of 2019 [[Tulz]], [[Nobody (Nicolás Ale)|Nobody]], and [[Spooky (Miroslav Gochev)|Spooky]] left the team.

For 2020, the organization hired 2 former [[Furious Gaming]] players and 1 from [[INFINITY|Infinity Esports]]: [[Josedeodo]], [[Shadow (Facundo Cuello)|Shadow]], and [[Renyu]]. This roster reached playoffs but were defeated again by [[Isurus]] in a 3-1. This led to [[Renyu]]'s departure and [[Leza]]'s roleswap from mid to bot, while [[Aloned]] also joined the team. Reaching playoffs, they defeated [[Azules Esports]] 3-2, then they had their revenge eliminating [[Isurus]] in a 3-1 and finally, won the finals reversweeping [[All Knights]], winning 3-2 and classifying for the first time since 2017 to the World Championship.

Until 2024, they were the most decorated team in Latin America with 16 championships obtained, during their history as [[Lyon Gaming (2013 Latin American Team)|Lyon Gaming]], [[Seven Wars Lyon]], Rainbow7 and Movistar R7.<ref>[https://lolesports.com/article/medallero-hist-rico-en-latinoam-rica/blt92678f1a0ecf8cf6 Medallero histórico en Latinoamérica (Spanish)] ''lolesports.com''</ref>

== Trivia ==
* Third team to achieve a [[LLA]] back-to-back championship, after their wins during both 2023 splits.
* First and only Latin American team to have won a best-of series against a major region team.
